certification.question: What does certification mean, and what can I not do until then?
certification.answer:
Certification is an admin confirming your account is ready to work with children. Two things come before it: accepting your Gedu contract, and presenting a criminal record extract for working with children (rikosrekisteriote) that is less than six months old. You order the extract yourself from the Legal Register Centre. We keep no copy of it and record nothing out of it — only that an acceptable one was shown, and when. Your contract page shows where both of them stand.

Until you are certified you cannot be assigned to a group, and your Tools section stays closed: you cannot start an instant voice room, and you cannot reset Minecraft Education passwords. You also cannot email a session report to families or add photos to one.

Everything else is open now: signing in, My SOG, your profile and coverage areas, and reading and accepting the contract. Help is here whether or not you are certified — use the form above if you are waiting and want to know where you stand.

groupAssignment.question: How do I get assigned to a group?
groupAssignment.answer:
An admin assigns you. Assignments are made from a club, camp or event’s groups panel on the admin side — you cannot assign yourself, and there is no request to submit — and you can hold one group per club, camp or event.

Two things decide whether you appear as an option: your account has to be certified, and the admin picking a Gedu sees the languages you speak beside your name and can filter on them, so keeping your spoken languages up to date in your settings is what puts you in front of the right groups. Your coverage areas are for something else — finding you as a substitute when another Gedu cannot cover a session — so they are worth keeping current too.

There is no email when an assignment is made — the group and its next session appear on your My SOG the next time you open it.

takingAttendance.question: How do I take attendance?
takingAttendance.answer:
From your My SOG:

Open the club, camp or event you run. Its sessions are all listed on its page.Find the session and tap Edit.Attendance is the first thing in the editor: one row per gamer, each with Present and Absent.Mark every gamer on the list, then tap Save.

A row starts unmarked, and unmarked is a real third state rather than a quiet “absent”. Tapping an answer you have already chosen clears it again, so a wrong tap costs nothing, and the counter above the list tells you how many of the group you have marked so far.

You can save a half-marked sheet and finish it later — nothing you have already marked is lost. There is deliberately no “mark all present”: the register is also your confirmation that the session ran, and it is what you are paid on. Saving it does not finish the session on its own, though — the report and sending it to the families are the rest.

attendanceAlert.question: Why does my club still show a yellow “needs attention” mark?
attendanceAlert.answer:
Because that session still owes something. When a finished session is flagged, it is one of these four:

Every gamer on the group’s current roster is marked, present or absent.A session report has been written. Text you wrote in the plan beforehand counts as one, so revise it into what actually happened.That report has been sent to the families.On the last session of a run that requires creations, every member has one.

The first is by far the most common reason. Marking the gamers who turned up is only half the register — the ones who did not turn up need marking Absent, or their rows stay unmarked and the session stays flagged.

One other thing reopens a session you had already finished: a gamer who joins the group afterwards. Nobody has said yet whether they were there, so their row comes back unmarked and waits for you.

safeguardingConcern.question: I have a safeguarding concern mid-session — what do I do?
safeguardingConcern.answer:
Deal with the immediate situation first. In an online session you hold the moderator controls in the voice room: mute a microphone, lock it, or move someone into a private space away from the group. In person the product has no controls for this — you handle it in the room yourself. Either way, put it on record the same day, while it is fresh.

Every session has a staff note, marked for Gedus and admins, that families never see; it is where an incident, bullying or a worry about a gamer belongs. There is also a per-gamer note on the group roster that stays with that child in that group, session to session, and is likewise Gedu- and admin-only. Neither is visible to any family.

A note is a record, not an alert: nobody is paged by it, so anything urgent, or anything that needs someone beyond the group, goes to the office at {supportEmail} as well.

gamerNotArrived.question: A gamer has not arrived and the session has started — what can I do?
gamerNotArrived.answer:
First, be sure who is missing. Online, check who is actually in the room against your roster — the participant list only shows people who are connected right now, so a name missing from it is a gamer who has not made it in, and nothing marks that for you; you read it off the list. In person, the group’s roster is who should be there, and you check the room against it the same way.

To reach the family, open the group’s roster in the group workspace: each row carries the family’s contact email, which you copy with a tap, and there is a copy-all control above the list. You send from your own mail — there is no in-app message to a family, no text message, and no phone number on the roster.

Online, what you cannot do is admit a gamer yourself: entry is decided by our server on the gamer’s own request, and they need an active place in that group with the session window open. If they hold a place and still cannot get in, the fastest fix is usually on their side — allow the browser microphone access, close whatever else is using it, reload. If it is something we need to fix, mail the office at {supportEmail}.
